newsitem.title: UK: THE PROTEUS COLUMN - Enterprise Re, Sphere Drake.
newsitem.headline: THE PROTEUS COLUMN - Enterprise Re, Sphere Drake.

text.p: THE PROTEUS COLUMN
Insurers are becoming increasingly aware that companies, including those in their own industry, are looking to them to ease concern over exposure to losses on the financial markets.

The fact is demonstrated by two recent developments. First - the launch by a group of Bermudan insurers of Enterprise Re to provide a broad range of financial risk insurance programmes with a focus on coverage for insurance companies and reinsurers.

Second, this week's announcement by AIG of a programme for commercial accounts that integrates coverage of financial market exposures, such as losses in foreign exchange or commodities markets or interest-rate sensitive investments, with traditionally insured risks.

Enterprise Re describes its services as "strategic risk financing". It wants to focus on protecting clients' earnings and balance sheet from all risks. The focus of Enterprise Re's initial marketing efforts appears to be insurers and reinsurers.

For insurers and reinsurers, Enterprise Re coverage can include investment market losses that coincide with falls in surplus caused by catastrophe losses, unforeseen underwriting losses or a need to significantly increase loss reserves.
The coverage would be triggered if an insurer loses money because it is forced to cash out of investments when the assets are low in value.

The impact of the growth of such products may note mean the end of the insurance cycle, but if it catches on it should encourage greater efficiency across the industry, better use of resources to pay claims, and more use of longer-term higher-yield investments by the industry.
--oo0oo--
Last year Bermuda and London Market insurer Sphere Drake joined the ranks of those who have pulled out of marine insurance, having earlier withdrawn from the energy market.
Direct marine business accounted for 30 percent of premium income, but a six month study showed that its marine lines had historically performed poorly in comparison with other lines.
Instead it refocused its underwriting on reinsurance and specialty insurance lines, and the results published yesterday could be taken as an indication that the plan is working.

True, the company still predicts lower earnings in 1997. This is partly because of universal factors such as excess capacity and the competitive rating environment, but partly also because of costs stemming from the restructure.

However a look at the figures for the last quarter shows premiums from underwriting are on the increase, largely as a result of no claims bonuses on reinsurance protections following the favourable property catastrophe experience for the year.
The focus on profitability rather than volume may be beginning to work.
--OO0OO--
